messages:
olivia_support: FYI customer (acme-inc) reporting a hard-to-repro Next.js build + runtime failure when bundling our Node TS SDK. They see a build error about package subpath + then a 401 at runtime only on Vercel.
olivia_support: Repro steps they gave:
1) npx create-next-app@latest --use-npm app
2) npm i redwood-inference@1.2.4
3) import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference'
4) build and deploy to Vercel (app dir / turbopack)

olivia_support: Build error snippet they pasted:
```
Error: Package subpath './package.json' is not defined by "exports" in /workspace/node_modules/redwood-inference/package.json
at resolveExports (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:...)
at Function.Module._resolveFilename (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:...)
```

kevin_eng: which Node + npm + Next.js versions? also which bundler (turbopack vs webpack)?

olivia_support: Node 18.16, npm 9.6, Next 13.4 (app dir), turbopack on Vercel. They also said local dev (next dev) works, only next build -> vercel deploy fails and runtime 401: "Missing authentication header" when calling our hosted API.

nidhi_devex: this smells like an exports map resolution issue combined with bundler tree-shaking: turbopack resolves to the ESM entry but misses the packaged package.json (some bundlers expect ./package.json to be exported). Quick workaround: add `experimental: { esmExternals: false }` to next.config.js to force CJS resolution.

kevin_eng: can you paste package.json from their installed SDK? also which fields we publish (main/module/types/exports)?

olivia_support: they pasted this from node_modules/redwood-inference/package.json:
```
{
  "name": "redwood-inference",
  "version": "1.2.4",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.mjs.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "dist/index.mjs.js",
      "require": "dist/index.cjs.js"
    }
  }
}
```

nidhi_devex: exports doesn't list ./package.json or ./types — some bundlers attempt to import package.json for metadata (or resolve types path) and choke if it's not in exports. Also the runtime 401 could come from bundling away default headers because they picked the wrong entrypoint (esm builds that assume fetch polyfills). Workaround for customer: pin to 1.2.2 (which still had a flattened root file) or add the esmExternals false. They confirmed pinning to 1.2.2 fixed both build and runtime.

maria_engineering: ok thanks. Long-term fix: we should publish a patch that explicitly exports ./package.json and ./types, and include a `types` entrypoint in exports so bundlers can resolve declarations. Example exports block to publish:
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "dist/index.mjs.js",
    "require": "dist/index.cjs.js",
    "types": "dist/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./types": "dist/index.d.ts"
}
```

maria_engineering: also ensure published package includes dist/index.d.ts at the path and add a non-minified package.json in the tarball so tools that import it can read it.

kevin_eng: agreed. I'll cut 1.2.5 that adds the exports entries and an integration test against a Next.js build (turbopack + webpack) to prevent regressions. ETA ~48 hours. Will backport to a 1.2.4 hotfix if needed for enterprise customers.

olivia_support: customer asked for a temporary manifest they can use while we patch. I suggested adding to their next.config.js:
```
module.exports = {
  experimental: { esmExternals: false },
  webpack: (cfg) => {
    cfg.externals = cfg.externals || [];
    cfg.externals.push('redwood-inference');
    return cfg;
  }
};
```

kevin_eng: thanks. @maria_engineering can you review the PR before merge? I'm going to open it now.

release-bot: PR #2345 opened: "fix: exports map + publish types for Next.js/Turbopack consumers (1.2.5)" :github:

olivia_support: I'll follow up with the customer and offer the pin + the temporary next.config change if they can't wait. Closing loop once patch is out. :thumbsup:
